neighbours.label: the word just before an expected demonstrative in a fixed phrase ('along [those lines]', 'at precisely [that moment]', 'head in [that direction]', 'to [that effect]'); the opposite pole suppresses this/that/those
fire: She wanted a cottage, a cabin, or something along those lines for the summer.
The phone rang, and at exactly that moment the power failed.
He muttered something to that effect and left the room.
Other banks are likely to move in that same direction next year.
We need a bigger budget or something along those lines before we start.
The letter said she was resigning, or words to that effect.
Just at that very instant, the door flew open.
If prices keep rising, the market could go in that direction too.
quiet: She wanted to walk along the beach and collect shells for the summer.
The phone rang, and after a minute the power failed.
He muttered to his brother and left the room.
Other banks are likely to move their offices next year.
We need a bigger budget and more staff before we start.
The letter said she was resigning at the end of the month.
Just after dinner, the door flew open.
If prices keep rising, the market could fall sharply too.

notes: Card top: 'went under the name', 'head in that same direction', 'at precisely that moment', 'something along those lines', 'something to that effect'; + pole suppresses ' this', ' those', ' that'. Probe: 'something along those lines' 0.673, 'At precisely that moment' 0.319, 'head in that same direction' 0.317, 'something to that effect' 0.220; literal 'walked along the river' 0.002, 'under the bed' 0.004, 'head to the coast' 0.030.
